title: Building a Scalable Design System for Product Consistency
background: As the Tignis product suite grew, inconsistencies began appearing across different applications and features. Multiple teams were contributing UI elements independently, leading to duplicated work, visual inconsistencies, and slower development cycles. To address this, we initiated a project to create a scalable design system that would unify the interface across products while supporting the needs of both designers and developers.
role: I led the design and implementation of the design system. My responsibilities included auditing existing interfaces, defining reusable UI patterns, customizing Material UI to align with our brand, and collaborating closely with engineering to ensure the components were practical for real-world implementation.
design:
Design Process
Research & Audit
I began by conducting a comprehensive UI audit across existing applications to identify inconsistencies in typography, color usage, spacing, and component behaviors. I also interviewed developers to understand common friction points when implementing UI.
Ideation & System Architecture
Using the findings, I structured the design system around core foundations—color tokens, typography scales, spacing rules, and layout principles. From there, I designed reusable components such as buttons, form inputs, tables, navigation patterns, and data visualization elements.
Prototyping & Documentation
I built high-fidelity component libraries in Figma and documented usage guidelines, interaction states, and accessibility considerations. Each component was designed with scalability in mind, allowing variations without breaking consistency.
Implementation
To ensure adoption, I collaborated with engineering to build reusable React components using Material UI as the underlying framework. I customized themes and tokens so the UI matched our branding while still benefiting from Material UI’s robust foundation.
challenges:
Challenges & Solutions
One of the biggest challenges was balancing design flexibility with engineering efficiency. The product team wanted creative freedom, while developers needed predictable patterns.
To address this, I created component variants and clear usage guidelines, allowing teams to achieve visual diversity without breaking the system. I also ensured the React components mirrored the Figma library structure, reducing translation issues between design and code.
impact:
Outcomes / Impact
The design system significantly improved collaboration between design and engineering.
Key outcomes included:
Faster feature development through reusable components
Improved UI consistency across the product suite
Reduced design and engineering rework
Streamlined onboarding for new developers and designers
By establishing a shared system of design and code, we created a foundation that supported the product’s continued growth and scalability.

title: Implementing a User-Centered Design Process to Reduce Product Rework
background: Early product features were often built based on internal assumptions rather than validated user needs. This sometimes resulted in features requiring multiple revisions after release. To improve alignment with customer workflows and reduce costly rework, we adopted a more structured user-centered design process.
role: I introduced and led an iterative design workflow that emphasized early concept validation through prototypes and structured user feedback. I collaborated with product managers, engineers, and customers to ensure design decisions were informed by real-world usage.
design: Research /n I worked with product and customer success teams to gather qualitative insights from existing users. This included identifying common pain points, observing how users navigated the platform, and understanding their goals within the product. /n Ideation /n Based on these insights, I developed low-fidelity wireframes to explore multiple potential solutions. These early concepts allowed us to quickly iterate without committing to detailed visual design. /n Prototyping /n Once promising directions were identified, I created high-fidelity interactive prototypes in Figma. These prototypes simulated real workflows, allowing stakeholders and clients to experience the proposed features before development began. /n Testing & Feedback /n We conducted feedback sessions with internal stakeholders and select customers. Observing how users interacted with the prototypes helped identify usability issues early and refine the design before handoff to engineering.
challenges: A key challenge was shifting internal expectations. Some stakeholders initially preferred jumping straight to development rather than investing time in early validation. /n To address this, I demonstrated how prototype testing could quickly uncover usability issues that would be far more expensive to fix after implementation. As teams began seeing the value of early validation, this iterative approach became a standard part of the workflow.
impact: The new design process had several measurable benefits: /n Reduced feature rework during development /n Faster alignment between product, design, and engineering /n Increased confidence in product decisions before development investment /n Stronger alignment between product features and real user workflows /n By integrating research, prototyping, and validation into the development lifecycle, we were able to design solutions that more effectively addressed real customer needs.

title: Interactive Prototypes and Event Demonstrations for Product Growth
background: Tignis frequently engaged with potential clients at industry events such as SemiCon. However, demonstrating complex product capabilities in live environments posed challenges, particularly when reliable internet access was not guaranteed. To support sales and marketing efforts, we needed interactive prototypes that could effectively showcase the platform’s value in a controlled and reliable way.
role: I designed and developed interactive demo prototypes used in client presentations and industry events. These demos simulated key product workflows and allowed stakeholders to explore features in a guided, hands-on way.
design: Research & Planning /nI collaborated with sales, product, and leadership teams to identify the most compelling product features for prospective customers. We focused on scenarios that clearly demonstrated the platform’s value and differentiated it from competitors./n Ideation /n I mapped out demo flows that highlighted key capabilities while keeping the experience intuitive and engaging. These flows were designed to simulate realistic user scenarios rather than static feature showcases. /n Prototyping /n Using design tools and front-end development technologies, I created interactive prototypes that closely resembled the actual product experience. These included realistic data visualizations, navigation patterns, and workflows./n For certain events, I developed offline-capable versions of the demos to ensure reliable presentations regardless of connectivity./n Validation /n Before events, I tested the prototypes internally with sales and product teams to ensure they aligned with messaging and could be easily presented during client conversations.
challenges: The primary challenge was balancing technical realism with reliability. A full product demo could be unstable or dependent on live data, while a static mockup lacked interactivity./n The solution was to create interactive demo environments that simulated real product behavior while remaining fully controlled and stable, including offline functionality when necessary.
impact: These prototypes became valuable tools for both sales and product strategy./n Key outcomes included: /n More engaging product demonstrations at industry events/n Increased confidence during client presentations/n Stronger alignment between product capabilities and sales messaging/n Faster validation of potential product features before committing to development/n The demos also helped leadership visualize future product directions, influencing roadmap discussions and strategic decisions.

title: Accelerating UI Development with AI-Assisted Workflows
background: As product development accelerated, the team faced increasing pressure to deliver high-quality UI features quickly while maintaining consistency with the design system. To improve productivity and reduce repetitive implementation work, I began integrating AI-assisted development tools into the design and front-end workflow./n These tools included GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Claude, and ChatGPT.
role: I explored and implemented AI-assisted workflows that supported both design and front-end development tasks./n My responsibilities included:/n • Using AI tools to accelerate UI component implementation /n • Generating React component scaffolding /n• Improving documentation and code clarity/n• Supporting rapid prototyping during design exploration
design: Workflow Analysis\n I began by identifying areas where development time was spent on repetitive tasks, such as: /n• writing boilerplate React components /n • implementing common UI patterns /n • translating design specifications into code /n These tasks were ideal candidates for AI-assisted support. /n AI-Assisted Prototyping /n During early design exploration, I used AI tools to quickly generate prototype UI components that mirrored design concepts. /n This allowed faster iteration between design ideas and functional UI implementations. /n Implementation Support /n When building UI components, I used GitHub Copilot and Cursor to: /n • generate initial component structures /n • suggest Material UI implementations /n • assist with TypeScript and React patterns /n • automate repetitive styling logic /n I then refined and validated the code to ensure quality and maintainability.
challenges: The main challenge was ensuring AI-generated code met production standards./n To address this, I implemented a workflow where AI outputs were treated as starting points rather than final solutions, followed by: /n • manual refinement /n• code review participation /n • adherence to design system standards
impact: Integrating AI tools into the workflow significantly improved development efficiency./n Key benefits included: /n • Faster UI component implementation /n • Reduced time spent on repetitive coding tasks /n • Faster design-to-code iteration cycles /n • Increased experimentation during early design exploration /n This workflow also strengthened collaboration between design and engineering by enabling designers to contribute more directly to front-end implementation.

title: Client Prototype for Unbuilt Features
background: This is the description for Project One.
role: My role in this project was to lead the development team and oversee the implementation of the project.
design: My approach to this design involved creating a working prototype that would bring the envisioned features to life—giving clients a taste of how they would function once developed. The steps included:/n Stakeholder Meetings & Research/n I collaborated with product managers, developers, and sales teams to understand the core business goals of the features being demonstrated, and to gather all relevant user requirements. This also involved reviewing any available technical documentation to align the design with future build capabilities. /n Wireframing and User Flow Creation /n I created low-fidelity wireframes to outline the user flows, making sure the interactions were intuitive and user-friendly. This helped in simplifying complex ideas and ensuring the user journey was as seamless as possible./n High-Fidelity Prototyping /n Using Figma (or another tool), I created interactive, high-fidelity prototypes that simulated real-life interactions with the product. The focus was on making the user interface feel as realistic as possible without relying on any back-end functionality. /n Usability Testing & Iteration /n Although this was an early-stage prototype, I conducted quick usability tests within the team to gather feedback and ensure the key features were easy to navigate. I incorporated this feedback into the final prototype to enhance user experience before presenting it to the client. /n Client Presentation /n During the presentation, I walked the client through the prototype to showcase how the product would work once developed. I used the prototype to highlight key features and their potential value for the client’s workflow, demonstrating how the solution would meet their needs.
challenges: The client needed a way to demonstrate new, unbuilt features of their digital product to potential customers. These features were still in the design phase, and there was no working version available. The goal was to create an interactive, high-fidelity prototype that would allow stakeholders to visualize the product's capabilities and demonstrate its potential value to prospective customers./n The key challenges were:/n Demonstrating unbuilt features: How do you show something that doesn't yet exist?/n Communicating value effectively: How do we make potential clients understand the impact these features will have on their workflows?/n Ensuring clarity and realism: The prototype needed to be realistic enough to convince a client of its functionality, without misleading them about the product's current state.
impact: The interactive prototype was well-received by the client and their stakeholders./n The visual representation of the product’s future functionality helped the client clearly understand its value, making them more confident in their purchase decision./n As a result, the client signed a $2 million contract to move forward with the product, citing the prototype as a key factor in their decision-making process.
